statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-50646 (GHSA-gh2h-rhph-h37g) is a remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) when it parses crafted XAML. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.9 and fixed in 10.0.10 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gh2h-rhph-h37g, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/418, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.10/10.0.10.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none contains the WPF runtime assemblies PresentationFramework.dll, PresentationCore.dll or System.Xaml.dll, or a Windows Desktop runtime pack. What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. WPF runs only on Windows, so the vulnerable code path is not reached on these Linux builds.

What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. WPF runs only on Windows, so the vulnerable code path is not reached on these Linux builds.

CVE-2026-50646 (GHSA-gh2h-rhph-h37g) is a remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) when it parses specially crafted XAML input. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 9, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.17 and fixed in 9.0.18 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gh2h-rhph-h37g, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/418, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.18/9.0.18.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder or wpfgfx assembly or native library, no WPF build tasks, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB or smaller) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade that contains no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml, System.Xaml.xml and ReachFramework.xml) in reference packages, which describe the APIs and hold no code; and the WindowsDesktop transport nupkg, which carries only libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs and System.Diagnostics.EventLog) and no WPF code. Every PE file in the packages is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header; none is a native Windows executable or DLL, and the packages hold no Mach-O files. WPF is built only for Windows, so this owner does not contain the WPF component at all.
